#Goal
We found that in the nested transposon data there is pretty consistent scaling factor between contact and fraction of integrations.
Here I want to test whether that holds true for the neutral insert hopping data from the single LPs.

# Neutral inserts
```{r}
neutral_insert_local_ints = all_ints_comb %>%
  dplyr::filter(insert_name %in% c("LoxP", "CRE6") &
                  LP %in% c("N1", "-116 kb")&
                  type == "pool") %>%
  mutate(hopped = start != LP_coordinate,
         dist_to_LP = case_when(chr == LP_chr ~ start - LP_coordinate,
                                .default = NA),
         local_hop = abs(dist_to_LP) < distance_local_hop & !is.na(dist_to_LP) & hopped) %>% #dont include unhopped ints 
  dplyr::filter(local_hop)

 table(neutral_insert_local_ints$LP, neutral_insert_local_ints$experiment, useNA = 'ifany')
```
Two bioreps for -116kb CRE.
Two bioreps for N1 LoxP, but the old one (E1682) only has 65 local ints, so not really useable.
Just combine all experiments per LP

## 25kb bin size
Need to 'fill in' all the bins that have 0 contact. The 4C bins are on round numbers of 5000. So I need to start by finding the bin border close to the LP.
Then make a tibble with all possible bins +-2Mb from LP

```{r}
all_bin_borders_tib_25kb = all_single_LP %>%
  mutate(binwidth = 25000) %>%
  mutate(bin_border_at_LP = floor(start/binwidth)*binwidth,
         first_bin_border = bin_border_at_LP-2E6,
         last_bin_border =  bin_border_at_LP+2E6 + binwidth) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(bin = list(seq(first_bin_border, last_bin_border, by = binwidth))) %>%
  unnest(bin) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::rename(start_bin = bin) %>%
  mutate(end_bin = start_bin + binwidth,
         mid_bin = start_bin + binwidth/2,
         dist_from_LP = mid_bin - start,
         chromosome = str_remove(chr, "chr"))

all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb = all_bin_borders_tib_25kb %>%
  group_by(LP) %>%
  group_split()


names(all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb) = group_keys(group_by(all_bin_borders_tib_25kb, LP) )$LP
  
```

Link to SB counts
```{r}

SB_ints_by_contact_ls_25kb = lapply(c("-116 kb", "N1"), function(lp){
  intervals_4c_tib =  all_bin_borders_tib_ls_25kb[[lp]] %>%
    mutate(rownr = row_number())
  
  intervals_4c = intervals_4c_tib %>%
    select(chr, start_bin, end_bin, LP) %>%
    dplyr::rename(start = start_bin, end = end_bin) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  ints_in_cl = neutral_insert_local_ints %>% 
    uncount(read_count) %>% #count individual reads instead of integrations!
    filter(LP == lp) %>%
    select(chr, start, end) %>%
    GRanges()
  
  N_SB_ints_per_interval = findOverlaps(intervals_4c, ints_in_cl, ignore.strand = T) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    group_by(queryHits) %>%
    summarize(N_SB_reads = n())
  
  intervals_4c_tib %>%
    left_join(N_SB_ints_per_interval, join_by(rownr == queryHits)) %>%
    mutate(N_SB_reads = replace_na(N_SB_reads, 0))
})

#make one tibble and calculate fraction of ints
SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb = bind_rows(SB_ints_by_contact_ls_25kb) %>%
  left_join(virt_4C_tib_25kb_sel) %>%
  mutate(contact = na.replace(contact, 0)) %>%
  group_by(LP) %>%
  mutate(SB_reads_total = sum(N_SB_reads),
         fract_SB_reads = N_SB_reads / SB_reads_total
         )
```

## plot
```{r 4FG_contact_ints_neutral_insert}
SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb %>%
  mutate(dist_from_LP = abs(mid_bin - start)) %>%
  filter(contact > 0 & N_SB_reads> 0 & dist_from_LP ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = contact , y = fract_SB_reads)) +
  facet_wrap( ~ LP) +
  stat_cor(label.y.npc = 'top', vjust = 1, method = 'spearman') +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, stroke = NA)+
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm') +
  stat_regline_equation(label.y.npc = 0.8)+
  scale_x_log10()+
  scale_y_log10()+ 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position =  'none',
        aspect.ratio = 1)
  

```

Calculate slopes more exactly
```{r}
SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb_norm = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb %>%
  filter(contact > 0 & fract_SB_reads > 0 ) %>%
  mutate(log10_fract_reads = log10(fract_SB_reads),
         log10_contact = log10(contact))

contact_slope_tib = SB_ints_by_contact_tib_25kb_norm %>%
  group_by(LP) %>%
  summarize(slope = lm(log10_fract_reads ~ log10_contact)$coefficients['log10_contact'],
            intercept = lm(log10_fract_reads ~ log10_contact)$coefficients['(Intercept)'],
            pearson_cor = cor.test(log10_fract_reads, log10_contact, method = 'pearson')$estimate,
            pearson_pval = cor.test(log10_fract_reads, log10_contact, method = 'pearson')$p.val) 

contact_slope_tib
```
Slopes are 0.84 (-116 kb) and 0.76 (N1).
